name: Chang'e 3
first: First Chinese soft landing on the Moon; deployed Yutu, China's first lunar rover
description: Chang'e 3 was the third lander in CNSA's Chang'e programme and the first successful soft landing on the Moon since the Soviet Luna 24 in 1976 — a 37-year gap. The Long March 3B launched on a direct lunar trajectory in December 2013, with a single mid-course correction before lunar orbit insertion. The lander touched down in Mare Imbrium on 14 December and deployed the Yutu (Jade Rabbit) rover, which operated for 31 months despite a mobility failure ending its drive on lunar day 2. Chang'e 3's lander continued imaging for years afterward.

events.label: TLI
events.note: Direct trans-lunar injection on the LM-3B upper stage.

events.label: LANDING
events.note: Soft landing in Mare Imbrium 2013-12-14. First soft landing since Luna 24 (1976). Yutu rover deployed hours later.
